hook: Paul Scharre is a former Army Ranger turned defense policy analyst who leads work on autonomous weapons and AI strategy at the Center for a New American Security (CNAS). He served as a special operations reconnaissance team leader in the Army's 3rd Ranger Battalion, deploying multiple times to Iraq and Afghanistan, before moving into the Office of the Secretary of Defense. There he directed the working group that wrote DoD Directive 3000.09, the Pentagon's foundational policy on autonomy in weapons systems, and contributed to the 2010 Quadrennial Defense Review and the 2012 Defense Strategic Guidance. He holds a PhD in war studies from King's College London and a master's and bachelor's from Washington University in St. Louis. At CNAS he wrote Army of None, a 2018 book on autonomous weapons that won the William E. Colby Award and was named one of Bill Gates' top five books of the year, and Four Battlegrounds, a 2023 book on the global contest for AI power that led to his inclusion on TIME's inaugural TIME100/AI list.
